essence: Indexing a family recipe under all three inherited names made it findable across generations.
brief: A family’s recipe cards used three names for one cake. The editor retained each name and cross-referenced the entries, letting two siblings find the same page through different childhood words. The result served that family without asking it to settle on a single correct name.
understanding: An alphabetical index would have hidden the cake from relatives who remembered a different word for it. The disagreement between cards was useful information about how readers would search.
The editor added entries in each direction. In the first proof, two siblings followed different names to the same recipe page.
The example concerns one family’s collection. Its success lies in preserving access through familiar language, without claiming authority over the dish’s wider history or name.
